carousel.short: Whose door do you knock on to fix the pump?
carousel.long: Whose door do you knock on to fix the pump? A small developer is the building's first long-term owner.

carousel.short: One electric pump, inside one flat.
carousel.long: One electric pump, inside one flat. In a design review for an 11-unit infill project near Lisbon, most of the rainwater and sewage ran to an electric pump, and the pump sat inside one of the flats. That's a very bad decision.

The warranty is still ours. Within two or three years it becomes a maintenance issue. In Portugal, a developer selling to consumers answers for structural defects for ten years, and for other defects for five.

carousel.short: Diagram: Shared systems belong in shared space.
carousel.long: Diagram: Shared systems belong in shared space. Ask of every system where it fails, and whose door you knock on to fix it.

carousel.short: Simulate before you buy the premium kit.
carousel.long: Simulate before you buy the premium kit. The energy rating often hinges on a heat pump or solar more than on premium kit, so run the simulation first and spend after. If we try so hard and in the end we're a B anyway, what did we do?

carousel.short: Every building system gets two questions: where does it fail, and whose door do you knock on to…
carousel.long: Every building system gets two questions: where does it fail, and whose door do you knock on to fix it? Take the two questions into your next design review, and tell me what I missed.

quote.short: Quote card: "Strategically, we were putting the building's weakest link inside a private apartment."
quote.long: Quote card: "Strategically, we were putting the building's weakest link inside a private apartment." Asaf Eyzenkot, Suf Zen, founder of Realization.
